# Independent adversarial audit: fractional-factorial bulk certificate

Reviewer: finite_phase_drift_challenge. 2026-10-30. Internal mathematical review only. No external novelty certification.

## Verdict

The stated all-dimensional, single-linkage, fixed-width-bulk adjoint inequality passes this review. I found no mathematical defect in the killed-generator lemma, its simultaneous proper-support application, the exact factorial ratio, or the classwise escape argument. It is NOT a global recurrence theorem: the excluded coordinate strips remain infinite, and multiple linkage classes are not covered.

## 1. Hard finite-dimensional lemma

The positive-term estimate is valid uniformly up to zero coordinates: for 0≤t≤1 and alpha≤1/2, t^(1−alpha)−t≤(2/e)alpha. If E_alpha_n(z^n)≥0 and alpha_n→0, the total killing contribution is at most C alpha_n, so every killed vertex has zero limit coordinate. The limiting positive support is nonempty. A path from that support to a killed vertex must first leave it across an edge i→j with z_i>0 and z_j=0. Along the sequence z_i^n stays bounded below and L_n=log(z_i^n/z_j^n)→infinity (zero denominator treated directly). The magnitude of this single negative term divided by alpha_n is bounded below by a fixed positive multiple of

    min(L_n/2,(1−e^(−1))/alpha_n),

which diverges. All positive terms divided by alpha_n remain bounded. Other negative terms cannot cancel this. This proves the contradiction for all sufficiently small alpha, not merely along a chosen subsequence.

For fixed alpha in (0,1), the functional is continuous on the CLOSED simplex because both powers are strictly positive. Strict negativity therefore has a uniform negative maximum. Finitely many nonempty proper subsets of a strongly connected graph admit one common alpha. On a boundary support the full functional agrees exactly with the killed-subset functional: incoming edges from zero sources contribute zero, and edges into zero targets contribute their full negative source term. Uniform boundary negativity and its neighborhood follow by compactness.

Useful identification, not a literature equivalence claim: putting p=1/alpha and u_i=z_i^alpha gives E_alpha(z)=sum_i u_i^(p−1)(Qu)_i. The local theorem passes this audit under its explicit finite lifted-graph leakage hypothesis and positive differentiable forcing assumption. No positivity-of-polynomial-coefficients shortcut is needed. The source/target orientation, generalized-monomial derivative bounds, normalized eigenvalue/determinant step, inverse path formula, and final exact adjoint estimate all check. Global feedback and parameter compatibility remain unproved, as stated.

## 1. Lifted coercivity and normalization

With p=1/alpha, z_(r,a)=f_r^p a_a gives

    z_(r,a)^(1−alpha) z_(s,b)^alpha
      =f_r^(p−1) f_s a_a^(1−alpha) a_b^alpha.

Thus summing the killed-complex functional is exactly sum_r f_r^(p−1)(M f)_r, including same-phase reactions. Every lifted vertex has an outgoing edge because it can reach killing, so the finite source out-degree coefficients yield cW≤D≤CW. Choosing epsilon after the coercivity constant yields

    sum f_r^(p−1)(Bf)_r≤−gamma sum D_r f_r^p

with a uniform gamma>0. Setting omitted coordinates to zero preserves this for principal restrictions; p>1 makes the zero-coordinate factors harmless.

For C_I=D_I^−1 B_I, the inequality is weighted ell-p dissipativity with weights D_I, exactly as claimed. An especially short rigorous spectral proof uses the nonnegative Perron eigenvector for the spectral abscissa of the finite Metzler matrix C_I, including reducible cases: substituting it into the inequality gives s(C_I)≤−gamma. Hence every eigenvalue has real part≤−gamma. The real determinant det(−C_I) is positive (real eigenvalues contribute positively and nonreal pairs contribute positive modulus squares), and its absolute value is at least gamma^|I|. # Independent audit: frozen boundary composition instability

Reviewer: finite_phase_drift_challenge, 2026-10-30. Internal mathematical audit, not external novelty certification.

## Verdict

The stated counterexample passes the full audit. It refutes the specified fixed-alpha, fixed-fugacity frozen-count finite-phase resolvent extension, for every finite B strip containing phases 0,1,4. It does not refute recurrence of the original network, nor every possible finite-dimensional correction representation.

## 1. Graph, drift, and unavoidable positive tilt

The connector joins zero, A+B, and 3A+4B in a directed cycle; the reversible fast chain joins all its other complexes to 3A+4B. Thus the complex graph is strongly connected. In species order (A,B,C), the vectors (1,1,0), (3,4,0), and (-1,0,1) are linearly independent (determinant 1), so the stoichiometric rank is exactly three.

The increasing-A fast rates, divided by (B)_4 C^3, approach 6+r+7r². The decreasing rates approach 12r+r²+r³. Their difference is exactly -(r-1)(r-2)(r-3).

For t>0,

    H=b(t−1)+d(t^−1−1)=(t−1)(b−d/t),

so its nonpositive interval is precisely the interval between 1 and d/b. On (1,2), b<d and nonpositivity requires t≥1; on (2,3), b>d and it requires t≤1. A strictly increasing t=k r^alpha cannot satisfy both conditions for every r. Therefore every fixed k>0 and alpha in (0,1) gives H>0 somewhere. Furthermore t→0 and d/t=O(r^(1−alpha))→0 as r↓0, so H→−6. A positive component of the open set {H>0} has a finite left boundary r0>0 with H(r0)=0. Taking r in that component sufficiently close to r0 yields 0<H(r)<r³. This selection is rigorous even if H has multiple components.

## 2. Exact principal block and characteristic asymptotics

Let c_A>0 be the fixed A fugacity. The positive connector entries in the ideal matrix on phases (0,1,4) are exactly

    g40=24 c_A^3 (A)_3^(1−alpha).
